title: Langroid Neo4jChatAgent runs LLM-generated Cypher on the RAG (read) path with no validation (prompt-to-Cypher injection)
sink: langroid/agent/special/neo4j/neo4j_chat_agent.py:Neo4jChatAgent.cypher_retrieval_tool -> read_query -> neo4j session.run(<llm_cypher>) (auto-commit; no read-only/validation gate)
attacker_story: An app builds a Langroid Neo4jChatAgent for graph RAG: the LLM emits a CypherRetrievalTool whose cypher_query is run against Neo4j to fetch context. In 0.65.4 the retrieval (read) handler passes the model's Cypher straight to read_query -> session.run(query), an AUTO-COMMIT transaction, with NO validation -- so a prompt injection (in the user turn, a tool result, or graph data the agent reads back via RAG) that steers the model into emitting a write/destructive Cypher (CREATE/MERGE/DELETE, or LOAD CSV / apoc.* / dbms.* for file/network/OS when those procedures are enabled) is executed verbatim. The read tool, meant for read-only RAG, performs arbitrary writes and (config-conditional) RCE. No model is needed to prove it: the scripted model stands in for the completion the injection would elicit; the finding is that the framework routes LLM Cypher to the DB with no read-only gate. GHSA-2pq5-3q89-j7cc mirrors the SQLChatAgent prompt-to-SQL bug CVE-2026-25879. Fixed in 0.65.5 by validate_cypher_query (cypher_validator.py): the retrieval path is restricted to read-only Cypher and both paths reject LOAD CSV / apoc.* / dbms.* / CALL db.* unless allow_dangerous_operations=True (default False).

scripted_model.interface: langroid's own MockLM (a LanguageModel, type=mock) set as the agent's llm via Neo4jChatAgentConfig.llm=MockLMConfig(default_response=<tool-call JSON>) -- the framework's real LLM interface
scripted_model.plugged_into: agent.llm_response(prompt) -> MockLM emits the CypherRetrievalTool JSON; agent.agent_response(llm_msg) -> the framework parses the tool and runs cypher_retrieval_tool (the sink)
scripted_model.behavior: returns the fixture tool-call verbatim, ignoring the prompt; proves the framework runs model-authored Cypher on the read path with no read-only gate, independent of model behaviour
scripted_model.may_assume: that some untrusted content could make a real graph-RAG model emit this completion -- in-shape output for a Neo4jChatAgent, i.e. a cypher_retrieval_tool call carrying a Cypher query; nothing more
scripted_model.may_not_assume: no privileged config (allow_dangerous_operations is left at its default False -- the advisory's point is that the read path still executes writes), no network, no attacker already on the DB; only that the model's tool call reaches the retrieval handler. The retrieval handler's pre-checks (schema fetched, database has data) model an ordinary RAG session and are set to their normal in-session state, not an attacker privilege.

canary.mechanism: a loopback Neo4j-compatible server (memgraph, bolt 127.0.0.1:7687) runs inside the same --network none container. The attack Cypher, routed through the READ handler, CREATEs a node (:ChainlabCanary {nonce:<nonce>}); the oracle opens its own bolt session and checks that a ChainlabCanary node with the per-trial nonce exists -- a real database side effect, never a string-shape check.
